$comment: Reviewed RustSec exceptions for the Buildmesh Rust dependency tree (issue #1541).
`cargo audit` treats unmaintained/unsound/yanked advisories as warnings rather than
vulnerabilities, and this repository's policy is that a warning must be either fixed or
reviewed here. Every entry carries an owner, a rationale, and a `reviewBy` date; the
`check-rust-advisories.mjs` gate fails an entry whose review date has passed, so an
exception cannot become permanent by neglect.
A `vulnerabilities` advisory (a real vulnerability, not a maintenance warning) is never
listed here: those must be fixed, which is why rustls RUSTSEC-2026-0285 was resolved in
the same change that introduced this file.
`yanked` is empty. Its only entry used to be `zip@4.6.1`, which was un-yanked upstream on
2026-10-16 (the crate's other 4.x releases remain yanked); a reverted yank stops being reported, and a
stale exception fails rather than lingering with a rationale that no longer describes the dependency
tree. `zip` left the tree entirely in issue #2438, which dropped the `zip` feature from
`tauri-plugin-updater` and with it the RUSTSEC-2026-0367/0368/0369 extraction advisories.
`zvariant`, `zvariant_derive` and `zbus_names` (RUSTSEC-2026-0370/0371/0372) are unmaintained
upstream because they were merged into zbus 6.0.0, and each advisory lists `patched = []`, so no
release of these crates clears it. All three reach the tree through one non-optional dependency —
`tauri-plugin-opener`'s `zbus ^5.9` for Linux/BSD — which no feature switch can disable and no
published plugin release has moved to zbus 6. This is the "no fixed release exists" case in
docs/development/supply-chain.md rather than a missed upgrade; the dated evidence is in
docs/archive/2026-10/rustsec-zbus-unmaintained-2026-10.md.

advisories.rationale: Unsound Iterator/DoubleEndedIterator impls in glib::VariantStrIter. glib is pulled in transitively by the GTK3 stack Tauri links on Linux; Buildmesh does not call VariantStrIter, and the crate cannot be upgraded without a Tauri GTK4 migration.

yaml-rust is unmaintained and is pulled in by syntect, which Buildmesh uses for syntax highlighting of diffs and transcripts. It parses theme files that ship inside the repository, not user-supplied YAML, and syntect has no unmaintained replacement with a maintained API surface.

bincode 1.x is unmaintained. It is reached transitively through Tauri and tauri-plugin-updater. The app's own persisted state uses SQLite and JSON, not bincode, so the unmaintained crate is not on a path this repository controls; a major-version bump belongs to the Tauri upgrade.
proc-macro-error is unmaintained and is a build-time-only macro helper in the transitive graph. It cannot affect a shipped artifact's run-time behaviour.

zvariant is unmaintained upstream: it was merged into zbus 6.0.0 as its `wire` module and the advisory lists no patched version, so no zvariant release clears it. `cargo tree -i zvariant --target all` gives the whole path — zvariant -> zbus -> tauri-plugin-opener -> buildmesh — and Buildmesh never names zvariant or zbus in its own code. zbus is a non-optional `cfg(any(target_os = "linux", ...dragonfly, freebsd, netbsd, openbsd))` dependency of the plugin, so no feature switch removes it, and as checked on 2026-10-17 neither tauri-plugin-opener 2.7.2 (highest stable) nor 3.0.0-alpha.3 requires zbus 6. The released artifacts are the Windows, macOS and Android installers/APK. The Linux target is compiled and tested by verify.yml's Rust jobs on ubuntu-latest, which are gated on needs: changes rather than running on every pull request, so a Linux compile is part of normal CI; the subtree is not linked into anything Buildmesh distributes. Clears when a tauri-plugin-opener release requires zbus 6 or later.

zbus_names is unmaintained upstream: it was merged into zbus 6.0.0 as its `names` module and the advisory lists no patched version, so no zbus_names release clears it. It arrives by the same single path as RUSTSEC-2026-0370 — zbus_names -> zbus -> tauri-plugin-opener -> buildmesh — through the plugin's non-optional Linux/BSD `zbus ^5.9` dependency, and Buildmesh has no direct use of it. No published tauri-plugin-opener release requires zbus 6 as checked on 2026-10-17 (2.7.2 and 3.0.0-alpha.3 both pin `zbus ^5.9`), so there is no upgrade that removes it. Nothing in a released artifact links it: Buildmesh ships Windows and macOS installers and a signed Android APK. Clears with the plugin's move to zbus 6.

zvariant_derive is unmaintained upstream: its derive macros moved into zbus 6.0.0 and the advisory lists no patched version, so no zvariant_derive release clears it. It reaches the tree only as zbus's own proc-macro dependency on the same path as RUSTSEC-2026-0370 — zvariant_derive -> zvariant -> zbus -> tauri-plugin-opener -> buildmesh — and Buildmesh uses no zbus derive macro directly. Because the plugin's `zbus ^5.9` Linux/BSD dependency is non-optional and, as checked on 2026-10-17, no published tauri-plugin-opener release has moved to zbus 6, there is no version bump that removes it. It is also a proc-macro, so it is build-time only and cannot affect a shipped artifact's run-time behaviour. Clears with the plugin's move to zbus 6.
